header.author: Papyri Graecae Magicae
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:magic:dclp:64429:grc, from papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (CC BY 3.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.1.12: Words run across lines; each English word is given on the line where it fits best. Line 12 begins with the end of a word from the line before (“from i-/t”). Line 20: the sign δ after (½) is unclear, perhaps the fraction ¼, perhaps an abbreviation for drachma. The article is written twice across lines 28–29. ἀρμενιακόν is rendered “Armenian blue”; κριμνοῦ (“coarse meal”) is uncertain in a dye recipe.

nodes.text: it, too, an undercoating for every
stone is serviceable.
Making of emerald.
Chrysocolla, weight (½) (drachma); Armenian blue,
weight (½) (drachma); urine of an uncorrupted boy,
(½) kotyle; of bull’s gall, the liquid part, the
two-thirds; mix them and put them into a little pot
together, and put in all the stones, so that
they weigh (½) (obol) and (½) δ each. And having put the lid
on the little pot, coat the lid round with clay,
and burn it on olive wood over a
gentle fire for six hours, boiling it. And if
this sign appears, the lid [turning] green,
burn it no longer, but let it cool and take
[it] off, and you will find them made. The
stones are crystal ones. And all crystal,
when boiled, changes its
colour.
Dye of 3 colours.
